dossier.public_summary: The dip repeats exactly at the star's 0.824-day spot rotation period and shows a large out-of-dip brightness swing and a 14% deep secondary eclipse, all pointing to an eclipsing stellar companion or spot harmonic rather than a planet. Duration is also too long for a planet around this small star.

reasons.why: Out-of-transit swing is much larger than the dip and highly significant, as expected for a close binary / spotted rotation, not a planet.
Dip period equals the star's spot period in every sector with very significant variability; a true planet would not typically lock exactly to the spin period with this amplitude.
reasons.value: rotation_d 0.824, signal_period_d 0.82441, signal_at_rotation_multiple 1, amplitude_ppm 18104 to 33760, false_alarm 0.0

reasons.why: A secondary eclipse with ~14% of the primary depth is well detected, inconsistent with a planet and indicates a stellar companion.
